2	name: mkdocs-site-bootstrap
3	description: Bootstrap a MkDocs Material documentation site for a repo and (optionally) deploy it to GitHub Pages — including pinned tooling via uv/PEP 723, a GitHub Actions workflow with paths-filter, llmstxt + copy-to-llm plugins so the site is LLM-friendly, and ongoing helper scripts to add new docs pages with auto-nav. 5	
6	# mkdocs-site-bootstrap
7	
8	Bootstrap and (optionally) deploy a MkDocs Material documentation site for a
9	repository, then keep helping the user add pages over time.
10	
11	This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
12	`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
13	asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
14	mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
15	starts fresh.
16	
17	## When to trigger
18	
19	- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
20	  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
21	- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
22	- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
23	  applied to a new project
24	- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
25	
26	## When NOT to trigger
27	
28	- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
29	- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
30	  unless the user is now reversing that decision
31	- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
32	- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`
33	
34	## Workflow
35	
36	### 1. Read preferences first
37	
38	Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
39	decision:
40	
41	```bash
42	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
43	  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
44	```
45	
46	Possible states:
47	
48	| State | Meaning | What to do |
49	|---|---|---|
50	| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
51	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
52	| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
53	| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |
54	
55	### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)
56	
57	Ask the user explicitly:
58	
59	1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
60	   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
61	2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
62	   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"
63	
64	Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:
65	
66	```bash
67	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
68	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
69	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
70	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
71	```
72	
73	If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
74	future invocations.
75	
76	### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)
77	
78	Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
79	`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
80	the short version:
81	
82	- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
83	  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
84	- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
85	  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
86	  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
87	  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
88	- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.
89	
90	Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.
91	
92	### 4. Scaffold
93	
94	Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
95	`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
96	`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
97	copy-to-llm.
98	
99	```bash
100	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
101	  --site-name "My Project" \
102	  --repo-slug owner/repo \
103	  --site-url https://owner.github.io/repo/
104	```
105	
106	Use `--dry-run` first to preview. The script always preserves any existing
107	files unless `--force` is passed.
108	
109	After scaffolding, run a local strict build to catch obvious issues:
110	
111	```bash
112	uv sync --extra docs
113	uv run mkdocs build --strict
114	```
115	
116	### 5. Enable Pages and trigger first deploy (consent gate)
117	
118	This calls the GitHub API (`gh api -X POST .../pages -f build_type=workflow`)
119	and then triggers the workflow. **Always confirm with the user first** —
120	say exactly which API call you're about to make and which repo it'll affect.
121	Only proceed on explicit yes.
122	
123	```bash
124	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/enable-pages.sh \
125	  --repo owner/repo
126	```
127	
128	Flags:
129	- `--dry-run` — print the `gh` calls without running them
130	- `--no-trigger` — enable Pages but don't run the workflow yet
131	
132	After success, set `pages_deployed=true` and `pages_enabled_at=$(date +%F)`
133	in preferences.
134	
135	### 6. Ongoing: add docs pages
136	
137	For each new doc the user wants, use the helper instead of hand-editing
138	`mkdocs.yml`:
139	
140	```bash
141	bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
142	  --section workflows \
143	  --title "My new workflow" \
144	  --slug my-new-workflow
145	```
146	
147	It creates `docs/<section>/<slug>.md` from the page template and inserts a
148	nav entry into `mkdocs.yml` under the matching section heading. Idempotent
149	— re-running with the same slug is a no-op.
150	
151	## Available scripts
152	
153	- **`scripts/check-preferences.sh`** — Read, set, or reset
154	  `.skills/preferences.yaml`. Always-safe to run.
155	  - Flags: `--get KEY`, `--set KEY=VALUE` (repeatable), `--reset NAMESPACE`,
156	    `--list`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
157	- **`scripts/init-docs-site.sh`** — Scaffold the site files.
158	  - Flags: `--site-name`, `--repo-slug`, `--site-url`, `--existing skip|wrap`,
159	    `--no-workflow`, `--dry-run`, `--force`.
160	- **`scripts/enable-pages.sh`** — Enable Pages and trigger first deploy via
161	  `gh api`. Requires `gh auth status` to pass first.
162	  - Flags: `--repo OWNER/REPO`, `--no-trigger`, `--dry-run`.
163	- **`scripts/add-docs-page.sh`** — Create a new page and insert it into
164	  `mkdocs.yml`'s nav.
165	  - Flags: `--section`, `--title`, `--slug`, `--template PATH`, `--dry-run`,
166	    `--force`.
167	
168	## Reference files
169	
170	- `references/preferences-schema.md` — Schema for
171	  `.skills/preferences.yaml` and conventions for cross-skill use. Read this
172	  whenever you're touching a preferences key for the first time.
173	- `references/existing-docs-handling.md` — Full decision tree for handling
174	  user's pre-existing `docs/` content without surprises. Read this **before
175	  step 3** of every fresh bootstrap.
176	- `references/docs-stack-recipe.md` — Verbatim stack recipe (mkdocs.yml,

178	  exactly is this stack?" or wants to apply pieces manually.
179	
180	## Bundled assets
181	
182	Templates the scripts copy from. Edit them here, not in the user's repo.
183	
184	- `assets/mkdocs.yml.template` — Material theme + llmstxt + copy-to-llm
185	  plugins + pymdownx.snippets, parameterized with `{{SITE_NAME}}`,
186	  `{{REPO_SLUG}}`, `{{SITE_URL}}`.
187	- `assets/pyproject.toml.template` — Minimal `[project]` block + the docs
188	  optional-deps group.
189	- `assets/docs-workflow.yml.template` — `.github/workflows/docs.yml` with
190	  paths filter, uv setup, strict build, Pages deploy.
191	- `assets/docs-skeleton/` — `index.md`, `getting-started.md`, `_snippets/`
192	  examples, `assets/copy-to-llm/` JS+CSS files copied from this repo.
193	- `assets/page.md.template` — Used by `add-docs-page.sh`.
194	
195	## Gotchas
196	
197	- **MkDocs strict mode rejects relative `.md` links pointing outside
198	  `docs/`.** Inside `docs/` → relative is fine. Outside `docs/` for
199	  `.md` files (e.g., linking to repo `TODO.md`) → use absolute GitHub URL.
200	  Outside `docs/` for directories or non-`.md` (`backlog/`, `pyproject.toml`)
201	  → relative is downgraded to INFO and tolerated. Templates already do this
202	  right; don't "fix" the absolute URLs.
203	- **`pymdownx.snippets` requires `_snippets/` in `not_in_nav:`** or strict
204	  mode complains about pages-not-in-nav. Template handles it.
205	- **`gh api -X POST .../pages` is idempotent for `build_type=workflow`** but
206	  errors on `404 Not Found` if the repo isn't pushed to GitHub yet. Check
207	  `gh repo view` succeeds before running `enable-pages.sh`.
208	- **The Pages deploy workflow needs `permissions: pages: write,
209	  id-token: write`** at the workflow level. Template has it; if you copy
210	  pieces into an existing workflow, don't lose this.
211	- **`copy-to-llm` plugin's `repo_url` is the SITE URL, not the GitHub URL.**
212	  Counter-intuitive name.
213	- **Don't auto-migrate existing user docs.** Always ask. Migrating someone's
214	  hand-curated `docs/` into a new structure is a high-trust action that
215	  should be the user's explicit decision, not the agent's default.
216	- **`.skills/preferences.yaml` is per-repo, not global.** Don't write it to
217	  `~/.skills/` or `~/.config/`. Each repo has its own decisions.
218	
219	## Updating an existing site (not bootstrapping)
220	
221	If `mkdocs.yml` already exists, this skill mostly defers — only
222	`add-docs-page.sh` and `check-preferences.sh` are useful. Don't try to
223	"upgrade" the user's mkdocs.yml without an explicit ask; their config may
224	have customizations the templates don't know about.
225
```

1	# Downstream docs stack recipe
2	
3	If you are building documentation for a project that consumes one of the
4	skills in this repo (especially [`project-knowledge-harness`](../skills/project-knowledge-harness.md)
5	or [`quantatitive-factor-researcher`](../skills/quantatitive-factor-researcher.md)),
6	this is the docs stack we recommend.
7	
8	It's the same stack this repo uses for its own docs, plus the optional
9	`mkdocstrings` layer for projects that have a Python API to document.
10	
11	## TL;DR
12	
13	```toml
14	# pyproject.toml
15	[project.optional-dependencies]
16	docs = [
17	  "mkdocs>=1.6",
18	  "mkdocs-material>=9.5",
19	  "mkdocstrings[python]>=0.24",   # only if you have a Python API
20	  "mkdocs-llmstxt>=0.1",
21	  "mkdocs-copy-to-llm>=0.1",
22	  "pymdown-extensions>=10.0",
23	]
24	```
25	
26	```bash
27	# Local preview
28	uv sync --extra docs
29	uv run mkdocs serve
30	
31	# Build static site
32	uv run mkdocs build --strict
33	```
34	
35	## Why this stack
36	
37	- **MkDocs + Material** — Markdown-first authoring, built-in search, a
38	  theme that doesn't need overrides for ~90% of projects, GitHub Pages
39	  deploy is one workflow file.
40	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — render API docs from Python docstrings via
41	  `::: package.module.symbol` directives in your Markdown. Only relevant
42	  if your project has a Python API; skip it otherwise.
43	- **`mkdocs-llmstxt`** — generates `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` so
44	  AI agents can discover and consume your docs without scraping HTML.
45	  Upstream is in maintenance mode but works fine; if it ever stops,
46	  swap in a hand-rolled post-build script.
47	- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm`** — adds "Copy to LLM / Open in ChatGPT / Open
48	  in Claude" buttons on every page. Pure UX sugar; harmless if your
49	  audience doesn't use it.
50	
51	## Why not these?
52	
53	- **Sphinx + Furo + MyST + autodoc.** Strictly more powerful, but the
54	  setup and maintenance cost is meaningful. Recommended only if AI-facing
55	  Markdown output becomes a first-class requirement, or if your project
56	  has the kind of cross-project reference graph Sphinx is built for.
57	- **pdoc.** Single-file API doc generator. Great for "I just want HTML
58	  for my package", but no good story for guides, conventions pages, or
59	  llms.txt.
60	- **Rspress.** Best-in-class for AI-native output, but it's
61	  Node-first / frontend-product-docs-first; Python API reference is a
62	  bolt-on. Not a fit unless you're already on the Node ecosystem.
63	- **Quarto.** Excellent for notebook / tutorial / research-report
64	  workflows; not optimized for Python library documentation.
65	
66	The longer version of this analysis (with the upstream-vs-inference
67	distinction made explicit) is preserved in the reference repo
68	[`mlflow-widgets/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/mlflow-widgets/blob/main/notes/docs-stack-evaluation.md).
69	
70	## Minimum `mkdocs.yml`
71	
72	```yaml
73	site_name: Your Project
74	site_description: One sentence about your project.
75	site_url: https://yourname.github.io/your-project/
76	repo_url: https://github.com/yourname/your-project
77	edit_uri: edit/main/docs/
78	
79	theme:
80	  name: material
81	  features:
82	    - navigation.instant
83	    - navigation.sections
84	    - navigation.indexes
85	    - search.suggest
86	    - content.code.copy
87	    - toc.follow
88	
89	plugins:
90	  - search
91	  - mkdocstrings:        # remove this block if no Python API
92	      handlers:
93	        python:
94	          paths: [src]
95	          options:
96	            show_source: true
97	            show_root_heading: true
98	            members_order: source
99	            docstring_style: google
100	            merge_init_into_class: true
101	  - llmstxt:
102	      full_output: llms-full.txt
103	      sections:
104	        Guides: [index.md, getting-started.md]
105	        API Reference: [reference/*.md]
106	  - copy-to-llm:
107	      repo_url: "https://yourname.github.io/your-project"
108	
109	markdown_extensions:
110	  - admonition
111	  - tables
112	  - toc:
113	      permalink: true
114	  - pymdownx.superfences
115	  - pymdownx.highlight
116	  - pymdownx.snippets:
117	      base_path: [., docs, docs/_snippets]
118	      check_paths: true
119	
120	nav:
121	  - Home: index.md
122	  - Getting Started: getting-started.md
123	  - API Reference:
124	      - Overview: reference/index.md
125	```
126	
127	## GitHub Pages workflow
128	
129	`.github/workflows/docs.yml`:
130	
131	```yaml
132	name: Docs
133	
134	on:
135	  push:
136	    branches: [main]
137	    paths:
138	      - 'docs/**'
139	      - 'mkdocs.yml'
140	      - 'pyproject.toml'
141	      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
142	  workflow_dispatch:
143	
144	permissions:
145	  contents: read
146	  pages: write
147	  id-token: write
148	
149	concurrency:
150	  group: pages
151	  cancel-in-progress: true
152	
153	jobs:
154	  build:
155	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
156	    steps:
157	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
158	      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v5
159	        with:
160	          enable-cache: true
161	      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
162	        with:
163	          python-version: "3.13"
164	      - run: uv sync --extra docs
165	      - run: uv run mkdocs build --strict
166	      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
167	        with:
168	          path: site
169	
170	  deploy:
171	    needs: build
172	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
173	    environment:
174	      name: github-pages
175	      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
176	    steps:
177	      - id: deployment
178	        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v5
179	```
180	
181	You also need to enable Pages in your repo settings: **Settings → Pages
182	→ Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions**. One-time setup.
183	
184	## Linking rules inside `docs/`
185	
186	`mkdocs build --strict` enforces these rules. Knowing them up front
187	saves an afternoon:
188	
189	- Links **between files inside `docs/`** → relative paths (e.g.
190	  `[scripts](../reference/scripts.md)`).
191	- Links to **`.md` files outside `docs/`** → absolute GitHub URL
192	  (e.g. `https://github.com/yourname/your-project/blob/main/TODO.md`).
193	  Relative paths to `.md` files outside `docs/` are rejected by
194	  `--strict`.
195	- Links to **directories or non-`.md` files outside `docs/`** → relative
196	  paths are tolerated (downgraded to INFO).
197	
198	If you want stricter validation (catch broken anchors too):
199	
200	```yaml
201	validation:
202	  links:
203	    not_found: warn
204	    anchors: warn
205	```
206	
207	## What this repo skips and why
208	
209	- **`mkdocstrings[python]`** — there's no Python API to document. We
210	  installed everything else from the recipe to keep the patterns aligned
211	  with downstream projects.
212	- **Versioned docs (e.g. `mike`)** — single-version docs are enough for
213	  a personal skills collection. Add `mike` if you ever need to keep
214	  docs for old releases live.
215
```

 `./skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md`

```text
1	# `.skills/preferences.yaml` schema
2	
3	Per-repo preferences file used by `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and any future
4	skill that needs to remember a user decision across sessions.
5	
6	## Location
7	
8	Always at `<repo-root>/.skills/preferences.yaml`. **Per-repo, not global.**
9	Each repository carries its own decisions; never write to `~/.skills/` or
10	`~/.config/`.
11	
12	The directory is created on first write. Add `.skills/preferences.yaml` to
13	`.gitignore` if the user prefers it private, but the default assumption is
14	that it's committed (decisions about *this repo's tooling* belong in the
15	repo).
16	
17	## Top-level structure
18	
19	```yaml
20	# .skills/preferences.yaml
21	# Decisions recorded by skills. Each top-level key is a skill namespace.
22	
23	mkdocs_site_bootstrap:
24	  enabled: true                  # null = never asked, true = opted in, false = opted out
25	  decided_at: 2026-04-23
26	  stack: mkdocs-material         # which docs stack variant
27	  auto_deploy: true              # deploy via GitHub Actions on push
28	  pages_deployed: true           # has the first deploy succeeded
29	  pages_enabled_at: 2026-04-23
30	  existing_docs_decision: skipped  # skipped | wrapped | none
31	  site_url: https://owner.github.io/repo/
32	  repo_slug: owner/repo
33	
34	# Future skills add their own top-level keys with the same shape.
35	# example_other_skill:
36	#   enabled: true
37	#   decided_at: 2026-05-01
38	```
39	
40	## Conventions for skill namespaces
41	
42	- **Namespace key matches the skill's directory name** with `-` → `_`
43	  (YAML-friendly): `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` → `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`.
44	- **Always include `enabled` and `decided_at`.** These are the universal
45	  fields. `enabled` is the consent state; `decided_at` lets the agent see
46	  how stale the decision is.
47	- **Don't store secrets.** This file is meant to be safely committable.
48	  API tokens, passwords, etc. go in `.env` (gitignored) or in CI secrets.
49	- **Don't store derived state.** Anything reproducible from other files
50	  (e.g., "is mkdocs.yml present") should be re-checked, not cached. Only
51	  store decisions and timestamps.
52	
53	## Three-state semantics for `enabled`
54	
55	| Value | Meaning | Agent behavior |
56	|---|---|---|
57	| key absent or `null` | Never asked | Run the interview |
58	| `true` | User opted in | Proceed without re-asking |
59	| `false` | User opted out | Don't pester. If the user is now asking for it, confirm they want to reverse the decision, then `--reset` and re-interview |
60	
61	This three-state model is why we don't use a marker file (presence-only)
62	or a boolean (only two states). The "never asked" state matters.
63	
64	## Reading and writing
65	
66	Always go through `scripts/check-preferences.sh` rather than parsing the YAML
67	yourself. It handles:
68	
69	- Creating the file and `.skills/` dir if missing
70	- Preserving the comment header
71	- Atomic writes (write to `.tmp`, then `mv`)
72	- Friendly errors for malformed input
73	
74	```bash
75	# Read one key
76	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled
77	
78	# Set one or more keys
79	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
80	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
81	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.decided_at=2026-04-23
82	
83	# Reset an entire skill namespace (returns to "never asked" state)
84	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
85	
86	# Dump everything
87	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --list
88	```
89	
90	The script supports `--json` for structured output that an agent can parse
91	reliably.
92	
93	## When to reset
94	
95	The user explicitly says one of:
96	
97	- "I changed my mind about <skill>" → `--reset <namespace>`
98	- "Stop nagging me about docs" → `--set <namespace>.enabled=false`
99	- "Re-ask me next time" → `--reset <namespace>`
100	
101	Don't reset proactively. The whole point is to *avoid* re-asking.
102	
103	## Cross-skill coordination
104	
105	Two skills shouldn't share namespace keys. If `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` and
106	some hypothetical `docs-publisher` skill both care about whether a docs site
107	exists, the answer is to **detect from the filesystem** (does `mkdocs.yml`
108	exist?), not to share a preference key. Preferences record *intent*; the
109	filesystem records *state*.
110	
111	## Schema versioning
112	
113	If we ever need to change the shape, add a top-level `schema_version: 1`
114	key and bump it. Until then, treat the schema as version 0 / implicit.
115	
116	## Validation
117	
118	`check-preferences.sh --validate` is a future addition (not yet implemented).
119	For now, trust the script's writes and don't hand-edit the file unless you
120	re-read it after to verify.
121
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-04-28 07:32:28Z)**_

可以做，而且和現有 skill 的「consent-gated + 後續可加頁面」結構契合。先給結論再講做法。

**建議：預設僅 English，提供「之後加語言」的明確路徑（Approach A）**，而不是一開始就強塞雙語 scaffold。理由：多數使用者只要英文，雙語會讓 base template、`llms.txt` sections、`copy-to-llm` 按鈕、`nav` 全部分支化，維護成本明顯升高；而 `mkdocs-static-i18n`（squidfunk 在那則 discussion 推薦的方式）本身就支援後加，retrofit 成本低。

**具體要落地的東西：**

1. `references/i18n-guide.md`（新檔）— 涵蓋 `theme.language`、`plugins.i18n` 兩種 `docs_structure` (`suffix` vs `folder`) 的取捨、`nav_translations`、與 `llmstxt`/`copy-to-llm` 的互動注意事項，並把「中文頁面保留英文原文」寫成硬規則：
   > 在 `zh-TW` 頁面，技術名詞**首次出現時** 以中文（English original）格式呈現，例：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」；後續只需中文。**不自創翻譯**；若無公認譯名則直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`）。代碼、API、CLI flag、套件名一律不翻。
2. `scripts/add-language.sh`（新檔）— 對既有站點 idempotent 加一個語言：插入/合併 `plugins.i18n` 區塊、依選擇建立 `docs/zh-TW/` 或 `*.zh-TW.md` 鏡像、把 `theme.language` 設成預設語言、補上對應的 `nav_translations`。`--dry-run` / `--lang zh-TW` / `--structure suffix|folder`。
3. `init-docs-site.sh` 加可選 `--languages en,zh-TW`（預設 `en`）作為「我從第一天就要雙語」的快速路徑——但僅僅是呼叫 `add-language.sh`，不在主 template 內 fork 出雙語版本。
4. 偏好檔擴充：`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages: [en]`、`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms: true`、`mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure: suffix`。`add-docs-page.sh` 在語言>1 時，依 `keep_english_terms` 把那條 terminology rule 以 admonition 形式注入到新建的非 English 頁頭部，提醒人類/agent 別亂翻。
5. SKILL.md 的 trigger phrases 增補：「雙語 docs」、「add Traditional Chinese」、「i18n」、「multilingual」、「zh-TW」。

**主要 trade-off**：A 的代價是雙語使用者要多跑一個 `add-language.sh`；B（一開始就雙語）省那一步但讓 default template 變複雜，且 `llmstxt` 是否 per-language 輸出、`copy-to-llm` 按鈕文字是否翻譯這些細節必須一次想清楚——而我覺得這些細節更適合在 i18n-guide 裡寫成 recipe，而不是寫死在 template 內。

1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
36	  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
37	  filesystem.
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
46	  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
47	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
48	  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
49	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
50	  content is already there.
51	
52	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
53	
54	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
55	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
56	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
57	  has been asked once.
58	
59	## What "non-hidden files" means
60	
61	For the purposes of this check:
62	
63	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
64	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
65	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
66	  "no existing content".
67	
68	Implementation hint:
69	
70	```bash
71	find docs -type f \
72	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
73	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
74	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
75	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
76	  | head -50
77	```
78	
79	## Things this skill must NOT do
80	
81	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
82	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
83	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
84	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
85	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
86	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
87	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
88	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
89	  breaks rendering.
90	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
91	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
92	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
93	
94	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
95	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
96	
97	## After bootstrap
98	
99	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
100	for option a) and report:
101	
102	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
103	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
104	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
105	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
106	
107	## Recording the decision
108	
109	```bash
110	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
111	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
112	```
113	
114	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
115	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
116
```

**When adding zh-TW (or any non-default language), how should translated pages be laid out on disk?**

Options:
- **Suffix siblings (Recommended)** - docs/index.md + docs/index.zh-TW.md sit side-by-side. Default-language file unchanged; translations are sibling files. Easier retrofit — no existing-file moves required, MkDocs default linking still works.
- **Per-language folders** - docs/en/ + docs/zh-TW/ as parallel trees. Cleaner mental model when a site is heavily multilingual; mandatory file moves at retrofit (every existing English page moves into docs/en/).
- **Let user pick at runtime** - Both modes implemented; add-language.sh exposes --structure suffix|folder, default suffix. More code to write & test, but no opinionated default.

- **Add --languages to init too** - init-docs-site.sh --languages en,zh-TW does both in one shot (internally calls add-language.sh for each non-default). Convenience for users who know from day 1 they want bilingual.

# Plan — Bilingual docs (zh-TW) support for `mkdocs-site-bootstrap`

## Context

**Why this change.** The `mkdocs-site-bootstrap` skill currently scaffolds a
mono-lingual MkDocs Material site. The user (a zh-TW speaker working primarily in
English) wants to be able to publish the same docs in Traditional Chinese, but
keep the choice opt-in: most projects start English-only, and a language can be
added later without re-scaffolding. There is also a hard preference about
**terminology** in Chinese pages: technical terms must keep their English
originals (no invented translations), so future writers — human or agent —
don't introduce ambiguity.

**Reference upstream.** Material for MkDocs covers two concerns separately:
[`theme.language`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/)
configures UI strings (single value), while content translation is handled by
the [`mkdocs-static-i18n`](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/discussions/2346)
plugin. We use both.

**Decisions already made (this session):**

- **Approach A — retrofit, not bake-in.** `init-docs-site.sh` stays English-only.
  A new `add-language.sh` does the i18n retrofit. Trade-off: bilingual users run
  one extra script. Win: base template, base CI, base `llms.txt` config stay
  unchanged for the 90% of users who only want English.
- **`docs_structure: suffix`** — translated files are siblings (`index.md` +
  `index.zh-TW.md`), not parallel trees. Retrofit needs **zero file moves** to
  existing English content; relative links inside `docs/` keep working.
- **Default language code: `en`.** Matches Material's own examples and
  `mkdocs-static-i18n` defaults.

**Intended outcome.** After this change, a user can:

1. Run `init-docs-site.sh` and get an English-only site (unchanged behaviour).
2. Later run `add-language.sh --lang zh-TW` to retrofit i18n: the script
   inserts the `i18n` plugin block into `mkdocs.yml`, creates stub
   `*.zh-TW.md` siblings of every existing default-language page, and records
   the choice in `.skills/preferences.yaml`.
3. Run `add-docs-page.sh --section X --title Y` and — if any non-default
   languages are configured — get parallel stubs with the terminology-rule
   admonition pre-injected at the top of each non-default-language stub.

## Approach summary (Approach A)

Add a single new script (`add-language.sh`), one new reference doc
(`references/i18n-guide.md`), three small `assets/` template additions, two
new preference keys, and minor edits to `add-docs-page.sh` + SKILL.md. The
existing `init-docs-site.sh`, `mkdocs.yml.template`, and
`docs-workflow.yml.template` are **not** modified — keeping the
English-only path byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Files to create

### 1. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh` (new)

Idempotent retrofit script. Bash 3.2 compatible. Same conventions as the other
scripts in `scripts/` (set -euo pipefail, `--dry-run`, `--help`, structured JSON
on success, `log()`/`die()` helpers).

**CLI surface:**

\```text
add-language.sh --lang LANG [OPTIONS]

Required:
  --lang LANG          Language code to add (e.g. zh-TW, ja, fr).

Options:
  --name NAME          Display name (default: derived from LANG, e.g. zh-TW → "繁體中文 (zh-TW)").
  --default-lang LANG  Override default language (default: en, must already be the existing site's language).
  --target-dir DIR     Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
  --no-stubs           Skip creating *.LANG.md sibling stubs for existing pages.
  --dry-run            Print actions without writing.
  --force              Overwrite existing stubs (default: skip existing).
  --help, -h
\```

**What it does (in order, all idempotent):**

1. **Locate `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD (mirror logic in
   `add-docs-page.sh:77-84`). Fail fast if missing.
2. **Detect existing i18n state.** If `.plugins[].i18n` already exists, read
   the current `languages:` list and merge the new lang in (no-op if already
   present). Otherwise insert a fresh `plugins.i18n` block before `plugins.search`.
3. **Set `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires this).
4. **Insert `pymdownx.snippets` `not_in_nav` entry** for `*.<LANG>.md` if
   needed — actually not needed with `suffix` structure; `mkdocs-static-i18n`
   handles nav routing per language. Document this in the i18n guide.
5. **Create stub `*.<LANG>.md` siblings** for every existing markdown file
   under `docs/` (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`). Each stub:
   - Copies title from the source page (`# <Title>` first line).
   - Prepends the **terminology-rule admonition** (if `LANG != default`).
   - Contains a `!!! warning "Translation pending"` body so it's obviously a
     stub at render time.
6. **Update preferences:**
   \```bash
   check-preferences.sh \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=[en, zh-TW]" \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true" \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix"
   \```
7. **Print structured success JSON:**
   `{"lang":"zh-TW","stubs_created":N,"existing":M,"languages":["en","zh-TW"]}`.

**Exit codes:** 0 success, 1 invalid args, 2 mkdocs.yml not found, 3 refusing
to overwrite, 4 yq error.

**Reuses:**
- `yq` invocation pattern from `add-docs-page.sh:137-150` (same atomic `.tmp.$$`
  → `mv` write).
- `check-preferences.sh` for the preference writes (already supports nested
  arrays per Explore-agent finding: `--set "key=[en, zh-TW]"`).
- `log()`/`die()` helpers — copy verbatim from `add-language.sh` siblings.

### 2. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/i18n-guide.md` (new)

~150 lines. Sections:

1. **TL;DR** — `add-language.sh --lang zh-TW`, what it touches, where to write
   the actual translation.
2. **Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure** — what we picked and why
   (no file moves for retrofit; relative links still work; per-page opt-in to
   translation).
3. **Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement).** Verbatim:
   > 在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞**首次出現時**以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，
   > 例如：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」；後續同段內可僅用中文。
   > **不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
   > `mkdocs-static-i18n`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。
4. **What `add-language.sh` does** — step-by-step mirror of the script flow,
   for users who want to do it by hand.
5. **`theme.language` vs plugin `languages`** — the two are different; show
   both.
6. **`nav_translations`** — how to translate section titles (lives under the
   plugin's per-language config).
7. **Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`:** explicit notes —
   - `llmstxt` will pick up all `.md` files including `*.zh-TW.md`. If you want
     per-language `llms.txt`, drop `llmstxt` for zh-TW (the plugin doesn't
     support per-language sections out of the box) — document as a known limit.
   - `copy-to-llm` button text is currently English-only; translation requires
     a separate config and is out of scope for this retrofit.
8. **Removing a language** — `mkdocs-static-i18n` graceful-removal recipe
   (delete the plugin entry, optionally delete the `*.<LANG>.md` files).
9. **Reset path** — `check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap` if the
   user wants to start over.

### 3. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets/translation-stub.md.template` (new)

Used by `add-language.sh` step 5 when generating stub siblings. Body:

\```markdown
# {{PAGE_TITLE}}

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**；代碼/API/CLI/套件名一律不翻。
    完整規則：see [i18n guide]({{I18N_GUIDE_URL}}).

!!! warning "Translation pending"
    這個頁面尚未翻譯。原文：[{{PAGE_TITLE}}]({{SOURCE_PAGE}})
\```

The admonition only renders for non-default languages — the script knows
because it's only invoked for non-default-language stubs.

### 4. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` (new)

The exact YAML block to inject into `mkdocs.yml` under `plugins:`. Used by
`add-language.sh` step 2. Stored as a snippet rather than inlined in the script
so it's diff-friendly and reusable from `references/i18n-guide.md` via
`pymdownx.snippets`.

\```yaml
- i18n:
    docs_structure: suffix
    fallback_to_default: true
    reconfigure_material: true
    reconfigure_search: true
    languages:
      - locale: en
        name: English
        default: true
      - locale: zh-TW
        name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
\```

## Files to modify

### 5. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh`

Two small additions:

- **Read `languages` preference at start.** If >1 language configured, after

- **New flag `--lang LANG`** to create only one specific language's page (used

- **Idempotency check** already greps for `$REL_PATH`

No change to nav-insertion logic: `mkdocs-static-i18n` reuses the single nav

without nav entries.

### 6. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/SKILL.md`

- Add **trigger phrases** to the workflow: "add Traditional Chinese",

### 7. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md`

Document the three new keys under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`:

\```yaml

keep_english_terms: true         # injects terminology admonition into non-default stubs
i18n_structure: suffix           # suffix | folder (currently only suffix supported)
\```

Note that `i18n_structure: folder` is **reserved but not implemented** — record

### 8. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets/pyproject.toml.template`

Add `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2` to the `docs` optional-deps group, but commented

`add-language.sh` un-comments the line on first run (idempotent grep + sed).

- **`folder` structure not implemented.** Only `suffix`. Schema reserves the
  key for future work. Document this in `i18n-guide.md`.

  admonition. Authors fill them in by hand.
- **`llmstxt` per-language not solved.** Documented as a known limit; for
  zh-TW pages, the per-page copy-to-LLM still works but `/llms.txt` will be
  English-centric. Acceptable for v1.
- **`copy-to-llm` button text not localised.** Out of scope.
- **UI strings beyond `theme.language`** (e.g. site footer, search
  placeholder) come from Material's translations. We rely on upstream's zh-TW
  catalog being adequate; if the user finds gaps, that's a Material upstream
  issue, not this skill's.

### 1. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh` (new)

Idempotent retrofit script. Bash 3.2 compatible. Same conventions as the other
scripts in `scripts/` (set -euo pipefail, `--dry-run`, `--help`, structured JSON
on success, `log()`/`die()` helpers).

**CLI surface:**

```text
add-language.sh --lang LANG [OPTIONS]

Required:
  --lang LANG          Language code to add (e.g. zh-TW, ja, fr).

Options:
  --name NAME          Display name (default: derived from LANG, e.g. zh-TW → "繁體中文 (zh-TW)").
  --default-lang LANG  Override default language (default: en, must already be the existing site's language).
  --target-dir DIR     Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
  --no-stubs           Skip creating *.LANG.md sibling stubs for existing pages.
  --dry-run            Print actions without writing.
  --force              Overwrite existing stubs (default: skip existing).
  --help, -h
```

**What it does (in order, all idempotent):**

1. **Locate `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD (mirror logic in
   `add-docs-page.sh:77-84`). Fail fast if missing.
2. **Detect existing i18n state.** If `.plugins[].i18n` already exists, read
   the current `languages:` list and merge the new lang in (no-op if already
   present). Otherwise insert a fresh `plugins.i18n` block before `plugins.search`.
3. **Set `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` requires this).
4. **Insert `pymdownx.snippets` `not_in_nav` entry** for `*.<LANG>.md` if
   needed — actually not needed with `suffix` structure; `mkdocs-static-i18n`
   handles nav routing per language. Document this in the i18n guide.
5. **Create stub `*.<LANG>.md` siblings** for every existing markdown file
   under `docs/` (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`). Each stub:
   - Copies title from the source page (`# <Title>` first line).
   - Prepends the **terminology-rule admonition** (if `LANG != default`).
   - Contains a `!!! warning "Translation pending"` body so it's obviously a
     stub at render time.
6. **Update preferences:**
   ```bash
   check-preferences.sh \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=[en, zh-TW]" \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true" \
     --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix"
   ```
7. **Print structured success JSON:**
   `{"lang":"zh-TW","stubs_created":N,"existing":M,"languages":["en","zh-TW"]}`.

**Exit codes:** 0 success, 1 invalid args, 2 mkdocs.yml not found, 3 refusing
to overwrite, 4 yq error.

**Reuses:**
- `yq` invocation pattern from `add-docs-page.sh:137-150` (same atomic `.tmp.$$`
  → `mv` write).
- `check-preferences.sh` for the preference writes (already supports nested
  arrays per Explore-agent finding: `--set "key=[en, zh-TW]"`).
- `log()`/`die()` helpers — copy verbatim from `add-language.sh` siblings.

### 2. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/i18n-guide.md` (new)

~150 lines. Sections:

1. **TL;DR** — `add-language.sh --lang zh-TW`, what it touches, where to write
   the actual translation.
2. **Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure** — what we picked and why
   (no file moves for retrofit; relative links still work; per-page opt-in to
   translation).
3. **Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement).** Verbatim:
   > 在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞**首次出現時**以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，
   > 例如：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」；後續同段內可僅用中文。
   > **不自創翻譯**——若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
   > `mkdocs-static-i18n`）。代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。
4. **What `add-language.sh` does** — step-by-step mirror of the script flow,
   for users who want to do it by hand.
5. **`theme.language` vs plugin `languages`** — the two are different; show
   both.
6. **`nav_translations`** — how to translate section titles (lives under the
   plugin's per-language config).
7. **Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`:** explicit notes —
   - `llmstxt` will pick up all `.md` files including `*.zh-TW.md`. If you want
     per-language `llms.txt`, drop `llmstxt` for zh-TW (the plugin doesn't
     support per-language sections out of the box) — document as a known limit.
   - `copy-to-llm` button text is currently English-only; translation requires
     a separate config and is out of scope for this retrofit.
8. **Removing a language** — `mkdocs-static-i18n` graceful-removal recipe
   (delete the plugin entry, optionally delete the `*.<LANG>.md` files).
9. **Reset path** — `check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap` if the
   user wants to start over.

### 3. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets/translation-stub.md.template` (new)

Used by `add-language.sh` step 5 when generating stub siblings. Body:

```markdown
# {{PAGE_TITLE}}

!!! note "Terminology rule (zh-TW pages)"
    技術名詞首次出現以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現，例：依賴注入
    (dependency injection)。**不自創翻譯**；代碼/API/CLI/套件名一律不翻。
    完整規則：see [i18n guide]({{I18N_GUIDE_URL}}).

!!! warning "Translation pending"
    這個頁面尚未翻譯。原文：[{{PAGE_TITLE}}]({{SOURCE_PAGE}})
```

The admonition only renders for non-default languages — the script knows
because it's only invoked for non-default-language stubs.

### 4. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/assets/i18n-plugin.yml.snippet` (new)

The exact YAML block to inject into `mkdocs.yml` under `plugins:`. Used by
`add-language.sh` step 2. Stored as a snippet rather than inlined in the script
so it's diff-friendly and reusable from `references/i18n-guide.md` via
`pymdownx.snippets`.

```yaml
- i18n:
    docs_structure: suffix
    fallback_to_default: true
    reconfigure_material: true
    reconfigure_search: true
    languages:
      - locale: en
        name: English
        default: true
      - locale: zh-TW
        name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
```

## Files to modify

### 5. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh`

Two small additions:

- **Read `languages` preference at start.** If >1 language configured, after
  creating the default-language page, also create `*.<LANG>.md` siblings for
  each non-default language using `assets/translation-stub.md.template`.
- **New flag `--lang LANG`** to create only one specific language's page (used
  when an author has just finished translating one specific page and wants to
  add a *new* page in zh-TW only — rare but cheap to support). Default
  behaviour: create the default-language page + stubs for all configured
  non-default languages.
- **Idempotency check** already greps for `$REL_PATH`
  (line 127) — extend to also check the language-suffixed paths.

No change to nav-insertion logic: `mkdocs-static-i18n` reuses the single nav
across languages; the `*.zh-TW.md` siblings are auto-discovered by the plugin
without nav entries.

### 7. `skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/references/preferences-schema.md`

Document the three new keys under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap`:

languages: [en, zh-TW]          # ordered list; first is default
keep_english_terms: true         # injects terminology admonition into non-default stubs

End-to-end smoke test in a throwaway directory:

```bash
# 1. Bootstrap an English-only site (regression: should behave as before).
mkdir /tmp/i18n-smoke && cd /tmp/i18n-smoke && git init
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/init-docs-site.sh \
  --site-name "Smoke" --site-url "https://x.io/" --repo-slug a/b
uv sync --extra docs
uv run mkdocs build --strict   # should pass — base template untouched

# 2. Retrofit zh-TW.
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh \
  --lang zh-TW --dry-run        # preview
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
# Expect: mkdocs.yml gains plugins.i18n block, *.zh-TW.md stubs appear,
# pyproject.toml uncomments mkdocs-static-i18n, preferences.yaml updated.

# 3. Re-sync deps and rebuild — must still pass --strict.
uv sync --extra docs
uv run mkdocs build --strict

# 4. Idempotency.
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
# Expect: "language already configured; 0 stubs created"

# 5. add-docs-page now creates parallel stubs.
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh \
  --section _root --title "About" --slug about
ls docs/about.md docs/about.zh-TW.md   # both exist
grep "Terminology rule" docs/about.zh-TW.md   # admonition injected

# 6. Local serve and eyeball language switcher.
uv run mkdocs serve   # check the language toggle in the Material header
```

Plus three quick checks against the skill itself:

- Run `bash scripts/add-language.sh --help` and confirm the help text matches
  the documented flags.
- `grep -n "mkdocs-static-i18n" skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/` returns hits
  in `i18n-guide.md`, `add-language.sh`, `pyproject.toml.template`, and
  `preferences-schema.md`.
- The repo's own `make docs-build` still works (sanity: we didn't accidentally
  break the agent-skills repo's own docs by touching shared assets).

## Known limitations / explicit non-goals

- **`folder` structure not implemented.** Only `suffix`. Schema reserves the
  key for future work. Document this in `i18n-guide.md`.
- **No automatic translation.** Stubs contain a "Translation pending" warning
  admonition. Authors fill them in by hand.
- **`llmstxt` per-language not solved.** Documented as a known limit; for
  zh-TW pages, the per-page copy-to-LLM still works but `/llms.txt` will be
  English-centric. Acceptable for v1.
- **`copy-to-llm` button text not localised.** Out of scope.
- **UI strings beyond `theme.language`** (e.g. site footer, search
  placeholder) come from Material's translations. We rely on upstream's zh-TW
  catalog being adequate; if the user finds gaps, that's a Material upstream
  issue, not this skill's.
```

1	# Handling existing `docs/` content
2	
3	The single highest-trust action this skill takes is deciding what to do with
4	content the user already has. Get it wrong and you can quietly destroy
5	hand-curated documentation. **Default behavior: ask, never auto-migrate.**
6	
7	## Decision tree
8	
9	Run this check **before** scaffolding anything:
10	
11	```
12	Does <repo>/mkdocs.yml exist?
13	├── YES → STOP. Report the path, don't overwrite. Suggest the user
14	│         either delete it first, or use add-docs-page.sh / check-preferences.sh
15	│         on the existing site.
16	└── NO  → continue
17	    Does <repo>/docs/ exist?
18	    ├── NO  → safe path. Scaffold from scratch with all templates.
19	    │         Record existing_docs_decision: none.
20	    └── YES → enumerate non-hidden files under docs/
21	        ├── 0 files (empty dir) → safe. Treat as "none".
22	        └── ≥1 files            → ASK the user. See "Three options" below.
23	```
24	
25	## Three options to present
26	
27	When the user has existing content under `docs/`, paste the file list and
28	present these three choices verbatim. Don't paraphrase — the wording matters
29	for an honest consent gate.
30	
31	### (a) Skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml`
32	
33	- Scaffold `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, the workflow, but **leave
34	  `docs/` untouched**.
35	- The generated `mkdocs.yml` will have `docs_dir: docs` pointing at their
36	  files and an **empty** `nav:` so MkDocs auto-generates the nav from the
37	  filesystem.
38	- Best for: user already organized their docs the way they want.
39	- Risk: their existing files may not pass `--strict` build (relative-link
40	  rules, missing snippets dir). Run `uv run mkdocs build` (without
41	  `--strict`) first and report any warnings.
42	
43	### (b) Wrap — add `mkdocs.yml` with my files explicitly in the nav
44	
45	- Same as (a), but **enumerate their existing markdown files into an
46	  explicit `nav:` block** so the user can see/reorder them later.
47	- Best for: user wants a starting nav structure but trusts the agent to
48	  pick a reasonable initial order (alphabetical by default).
49	- Don't add the standard `index.md` / `getting-started.md` skeleton — their
50	  content is already there.
51	
52	### (c) Manual — I'll reorganize first
53	
54	- Bail out cleanly. Don't write anything.
55	- Tell the user to re-run when ready.
56	- Record `existing_docs_decision: deferred` so a later run knows the user
57	  has been asked once.
58	
59	## What "non-hidden files" means
60	
61	For the purposes of this check:
62	
63	- Count: `*.md`, `*.html`, `*.txt`, any subdirectories with content.
64	- Don't count: dotfiles (`.DS_Store`, `.gitkeep`), `__pycache__`, `node_modules`.
65	- An empty directory or one containing only `.gitkeep` is treated as
66	  "no existing content".
67	
68	Implementation hint:
69	
70	```bash
71	find docs -type f \
72	  -not -path '*/\.*' \
73	  -not -name '.gitkeep' \
74	  -not -path '*/__pycache__/*' \
75	  -not -path '*/node_modules/*' \
76	  | head -50
77	```
78	
79	## Things this skill must NOT do
80	
81	- **Don't rename existing files.** Even "obvious" cleanups like
82	  `README.md → index.md` change git history and break user muscle memory.
83	- **Don't move files into subdirectories.** Users sometimes deliberately
84	  flatten or deliberately nest. Their structure stays.
85	- **Don't rewrite content.** No "I converted your relative links to
86	  absolute" without an explicit ask.
87	- **Don't add a frontmatter block to existing files.** Some users use
88	  `---` as a horizontal rule in markdown; assuming they want frontmatter
89	  breaks rendering.
90	- **Don't `git mv`.** Deferring file reorganization to the user means they
91	  decide whether to use `git mv` (preserves history) or plain `mv` (treats
92	  as new file). The skill shouldn't make that call.
93	
94	If the user explicitly says "yes, please move my README into docs/", that's
95	a separate action with its own consent — not part of bootstrap.
96	
97	## After bootstrap
98	
99	Whichever option was chosen, run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` (or non-strict
100	for option a) and report:
101	
102	- Any errors → must be fixed before deploy
103	- Any warnings → list them, let the user decide whether to fix now
104	- Any "info" messages about relative links to dirs outside `docs/` → these
105	  are tolerated by strict mode, mention them only briefly
106	
107	## Recording the decision
108	
109	```bash
110	bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
111	  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision=skipped
112	```
113	
114	Valid values: `none` (nothing was there), `skipped` (option a),
115	`wrapped` (option b), `deferred` (option c, user will re-run).
116
```
</details></tool-use>

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# add-language.sh — Retrofit a non-default language into an existing MkDocs site.
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible. Requires `yq` (mikefarah/yq v4+).
# Idempotent: re-running with the same --lang is a no-op.
#
# What it does (see references/i18n-guide.md for the full story):
#   1. Inserts (or augments) a `plugins.i18n` block in mkdocs.yml using
#      docs_structure: suffix.
#   2. Sets theme.language to the default language if not already set.
#   3. Creates *.<LANG>.md sibling stubs for every existing default-language
#      page, with the terminology-rule admonition pre-injected.
#   4. Records the choice in .skills/preferences.yaml.
#   5. Un-comments mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml if it's commented out.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SKILL_DIR="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
ASSETS="$SKILL_DIR/assets"

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: add-language.sh --lang LANG [OPTIONS]

Retrofit a non-default language into an existing MkDocs site (uses
mkdocs-static-i18n with docs_structure: suffix).

Required:
  --lang LANG          Language code to add (e.g. zh-TW, ja, fr, de).

Options:
  --name NAME          Display name (default: derived from LANG, e.g.
                       zh-TW → "繁體中文 (zh-TW)"). Falls back to LANG.
  --default-lang LANG  Default language already on the site (default: en).
                       Used to seed theme.language and i18n.languages[0].
  --target-dir DIR     Repo root (default: walk up from CWD looking for mkdocs.yml).
  --no-stubs           Skip creating *.<LANG>.md sibling stubs.
  --dry-run            Print actions without writing.
  --force              Overwrite existing *.<LANG>.md stubs (default: skip).
  --help, -h           Show this help and exit.

Examples:
  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW                              # add Traditional Chinese
  add-language.sh --lang ja --name "日本語"                 # add Japanese with custom name
  add-language.sh --lang zh-TW --dry-run                    # preview changes
  add-language.sh --lang fr --no-stubs                      # plugin only, no stubs

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  invalid arguments
  2  mkdocs.yml not found
  3  refusing to overwrite (use --force)
  4  yq error
EOF
}

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }
die()  { printf 'error: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit "${2:-1}"; }

LOCALE=""
LOCALE_NAME=""
DEFAULT_LANG="en"
TARGET=""
NO_STUBS=0
DRY_RUN=0
FORCE=0

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --lang)         LOCALE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --name)         LOCALE_NAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --default-lang) DEFAULT_LANG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --target-dir)   TARGET="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-stubs)     NO_STUBS=1; shift ;;
    --dry-run)      DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --force)        FORCE=1; shift ;;
    --help|-h)      usage; exit 0 ;;
    -*)             die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" 1 ;;
    *)              die "unexpected positional argument: $1" 1 ;;
  esac
done

[ -n "$LOCALE" ] || die "--lang is required (try --help)" 1
command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "yq not found in PATH (install: brew install yq)" 4

# --- Locate mkdocs.yml ---
if [ -z "$TARGET" ]; then
  cur="$(pwd)"
  while [ "$cur" != "/" ]; do
    if [ -f "$cur/mkdocs.yml" ]; then TARGET="$cur"; break; fi
    cur="$(dirname "$cur")"
  done
  [ -n "$TARGET" ] || die "could not find mkdocs.yml walking up from $(pwd)" 2
fi
MKDOCS="$TARGET/mkdocs.yml"
[ -f "$MKDOCS" ] || die "no mkdocs.yml in $TARGET" 2
DOCS_DIR="$TARGET/docs"

# --- Derive display name if not given ---
if [ -z "$LOCALE_NAME" ]; then
  case "$LOCALE" in
    zh-TW) LOCALE_NAME="繁體中文 (zh-TW)" ;;
    zh-CN) LOCALE_NAME="简体中文 (zh-CN)" ;;
    ja)    LOCALE_NAME="日本語 (ja)" ;;
    ko)    LOCALE_NAME="한국어 (ko)" ;;
    fr)    LOCALE_NAME="Français (fr)" ;;
    de)    LOCALE_NAME="Deutsch (de)" ;;
    es)    LOCALE_NAME="Español (es)" ;;
    pt)    LOCALE_NAME="Português (pt)" ;;
    it)    LOCALE_NAME="Italiano (it)" ;;
    en)    LOCALE_NAME="English" ;;
    *)     LOCALE_NAME="$LOCALE" ;;
  esac
fi

DEFAULT_NAME="English"
[ "$DEFAULT_LANG" = "en" ] || DEFAULT_NAME="$DEFAULT_LANG"

log "Target: $TARGET"
log "Locale: $LOCALE ($LOCALE_NAME)"
log "Default language: $DEFAULT_LANG"

# --- Detect current i18n state ---
HAS_I18N=$(yq '[.plugins[]? | select(type == "!!map") | keys | .[0]] | contains(["i18n"])' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
HAS_LOCALE="false"
if [ "$HAS_I18N" = "true" ]; then
  HAS_LOCALE=$(LOC="$LOCALE" yq '[.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale] | contains([env(LOC)])' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "false")
fi

log "i18n plugin present: $HAS_I18N"
log "Locale already configured: $HAS_LOCALE"

# --- yq write helper ---
yq_inplace() {
  local expr="$1"
  if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
    log "[dry-run] yq -i '$expr' $MKDOCS"
    return 0
  fi
  local tmp="${MKDOCS}.tmp.$$"
  yq "$expr" "$MKDOCS" > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "yq failed: $expr" 4; }
  mv "$tmp" "$MKDOCS"
}

# --- Step 1: insert / extend plugins.i18n ---
if [ "$HAS_I18N" = "false" ]; then
  log "Inserting plugins.i18n block..."
  yq_inplace "
    .plugins = (
      [{
        \"i18n\": {
          \"docs_structure\": \"suffix\",
          \"fallback_to_default\": true,
          \"reconfigure_material\": true,
          \"reconfigure_search\": true,
          \"languages\": [
            {\"locale\": \"$DEFAULT_LANG\", \"name\": \"$DEFAULT_NAME\", \"default\": true},
            {\"locale\": \"$LOCALE\", \"name\": \"$LOCALE_NAME\"}
          ]
        }
      }] + (.plugins // [])
    )
  "
elif [ "$HAS_LOCALE" = "false" ]; then
  log "Appending $LOCALE to existing plugins.i18n.languages..."
  yq_inplace "
    .plugins |= map(
      if has(\"i18n\") then
        .i18n.languages += [{\"locale\": \"$LOCALE\", \"name\": \"$LOCALE_NAME\"}]
      else
        .
      end
    )
  "
else
  log "Locale $LOCALE already in plugins.i18n.languages — no plugin change."
fi

# --- Step 2: set theme.language if missing ---
THEME_LANG=$(yq -r '.theme.language // ""' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [ -z "$THEME_LANG" ]; then
  log "Setting theme.language: $DEFAULT_LANG"
  yq_inplace ".theme.language = \"$DEFAULT_LANG\""
elif [ "$THEME_LANG" != "$DEFAULT_LANG" ]; then
  log "Note: theme.language is already '$THEME_LANG' (not '$DEFAULT_LANG'). Leaving as-is."
fi

# --- Step 3: collect all configured locales for stub-skipping ---
ALL_LOCALES=$(yq '.plugins[]? | select(has("i18n")) | .i18n.languages[].locale' "$MKDOCS" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ' || echo "$DEFAULT_LANG $LOCALE")
log "All configured locales: $ALL_LOCALES"

# --- Step 4: create *.LANG.md sibling stubs ---
STUBS_CREATED=0
STUBS_EXISTING=0
STUBS_SKIPPED=0
STUB_TEMPLATE="$ASSETS/translation-stub.md.template"

if [ "$NO_STUBS" = "1" ]; then
  log "Skipping stub creation (--no-stubs)."
elif [ ! -d "$DOCS_DIR" ]; then
  log "No docs/ dir — skipping stub creation."
elif [ ! -f "$STUB_TEMPLATE" ]; then
  die "stub template missing: $STUB_TEMPLATE" 4
else
  TMP_LIST="$(mktemp)"
  find "$DOCS_DIR" -type f -name '*.md' \
    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/_snippets/*" \
    -not -path "$DOCS_DIR/assets/*" \
    > "$TMP_LIST" 2>/dev/null || true

  while IFS= read -r src; do
    [ -z "$src" ] && continue
    base="${src%.md}"
    # Skip if this file is itself a locale-suffixed sibling.
    is_locale=0
    for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
      case "${base}" in
        *.$loc) is_locale=1; break ;;
      esac
    done
    [ "$is_locale" = "1" ] && { STUBS_SKIPPED=$((STUBS_SKIPPED + 1)); continue; }

    target="${base}.${LOCALE}.md"
    if [ -e "$target" ] && [ "$FORCE" = "0" ]; then
      STUBS_EXISTING=$((STUBS_EXISTING + 1))
      continue
    fi

    # Extract title from source (first '# ' heading), fallback to filename.
    src_title=$(grep -m1 '^# ' "$src" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^# *//' || true)
    [ -n "$src_title" ] || src_title="$(basename "$src" .md)"

    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
      log "[dry-run] create $target  (title: $src_title)"
    else
      sed -e "s|{{PAGE_TITLE}}|${src_title}|g" \
          -e "s|{{LANG}}|${LOCALE}|g" \
          "$STUB_TEMPLATE" > "$target"
    fi
    STUBS_CREATED=$((STUBS_CREATED + 1))
  done < "$TMP_LIST"
  rm -f "$TMP_LIST"
fi

log "Stubs: $STUBS_CREATED created, $STUBS_EXISTING already existed, $STUBS_SKIPPED skipped (locale-suffixed)"

# --- Step 5: update preferences ---
PREFS="$SKILL_DIR/scripts/check-preferences.sh"
ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="["
first=1
for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
  [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
  if [ "$first" = "1" ]; then
    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}\"$loc\""
    first=0
  else
    ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}, \"$loc\""
  fi
done
ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL="${ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL}]"

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL"
  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true"
  log "[dry-run] check-preferences.sh --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix"
else
  bash "$PREFS" \
    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=$ALL_LOCALES_LITERAL" \
    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.keep_english_terms=true" \
    --set "mkdocs_site_bootstrap.i18n_structure=suffix" \
    >/dev/null
fi

# --- Step 6: uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in pyproject.toml ---
PYPROJECT="$TARGET/pyproject.toml"
if [ -f "$PYPROJECT" ]; then
  if grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
    log "pyproject.toml already lists mkdocs-static-i18n — leaving alone."
  elif grep -qE '^[[:space:]]*#[[:space:]]*"mkdocs-static-i18n' "$PYPROJECT"; then
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
      log "[dry-run] uncomment mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
    else
      sed -i.bak -E 's|^([[:space:]]*)#[[:space:]]*("mkdocs-static-i18n[^"]*",)|\1\2|' "$PYPROJECT"
      rm -f "${PYPROJECT}.bak"
      log "Uncommented mkdocs-static-i18n in $PYPROJECT"
    fi
  else
    log "Note: mkdocs-static-i18n not found in $PYPROJECT. Add manually:"
    log '        "mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2",'
  fi
else
  log "Note: no pyproject.toml in $TARGET. Install mkdocs-static-i18n yourself."
fi

if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "1" ]; then
  log "Dry run complete."
  exit 0
fi

# --- Structured success output ---
LANGUAGES_JSON=$(printf '%s' "$ALL_LOCALES" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -v '^$' | yq -o=json -p=props -I=0 '[.] | .[]' 2>/dev/null | paste -sd, - 2>/dev/null || echo "")
if [ -z "$LANGUAGES_JSON" ]; then
  LANGUAGES_JSON=""
  for loc in $ALL_LOCALES; do
    [ -z "$loc" ] && continue
    if [ -z "$LANGUAGES_JSON" ]; then
      LANGUAGES_JSON="\"$loc\""
    else
      LANGUAGES_JSON="$LANGUAGES_JSON,\"$loc\""
    fi
  done
fi

printf '{"lang":"%s","stubs_created":%d,"stubs_existing":%d,"languages":[%s]}\n' \
  "$LOCALE" "$STUBS_CREATED" "$STUBS_EXISTING" "$LANGUAGES_JSON"

```md
# Bilingual / multi-language docs

How to add a non-English language (typically Traditional Chinese, `zh-TW`) to
a MkDocs Material site bootstrapped by this skill, and how to keep
terminology consistent so future contributors — human or agent — don't
introduce ambiguity.

## TL;DR

\```bash
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-language.sh --lang zh-TW
\```

That single command:

1. Inserts a `plugins.i18n` block into `mkdocs.yml` (using
   `mkdocs-static-i18n` with `docs_structure: suffix`).
2. Sets `theme.language: en` (or whatever the default is) so Material's
   built-in UI strings have a baseline.
3. Creates `*.zh-TW.md` sibling stubs for every existing markdown file under
   `docs/` (with the terminology-rule admonition pre-injected).
4. Records the choice in `.skills/preferences.yaml`.
5. Un-comments `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2` in `pyproject.toml`.

After it finishes, run:

\```bash
uv sync --extra docs
uv run mkdocs build --strict
\```

The Material header will gain a language switcher. Translate the stub bodies
when ready.

## Why `mkdocs-static-i18n` + suffix structure

[Squidfunk's recommended approach](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/discussions/2346)
for content translation is the
[`mkdocs-static-i18n`](https://github.com/ultrabug/mkdocs-static-i18n) plugin.
We use **`docs_structure: suffix`** rather than `folder` because:

- **Zero file moves on retrofit.** Existing `docs/index.md`,
  `docs/getting-started.md`, etc. stay where they are. The `folder` mode
  would force you to move every file into `docs/en/` first.
- **Relative links keep working.** Sibling files share the same directory.
- **Per-page opt-in to translation.** A page is only translated when
  `<page>.<lang>.md` exists; otherwise the plugin falls back to the default
  language (`fallback_to_default: true`).

The trade-off: directory listings get crowded once you have many languages.
For sites that grow to 5+ languages the `folder` structure starts to win on
readability — but you can migrate later.

## Terminology preservation rule (hard requirement)

This is the rule for any non-English page in a project that uses this skill:

> **在 zh-TW 頁面，技術名詞首次出現時，以「中文 (English original)」格式呈現。**
> 例：「依賴注入 (dependency injection)」、「型別檢查 (type checking)」。
> 後續同段內可只用中文。
>
> **不自創翻譯。** 若無公認譯名，直接保留英文（如 `embedding`、`tokenizer`、
> `mkdocs-static-i18n`、`pymdownx.snippets`）。
>
> **代碼、API 名、CLI flag、套件名、檔名一律不翻。**

The reason: Chinese-language tech writing has competing translations for
many terms (e.g. `cache` → 快取 / 緩存 / 暫存; `repository` → 倉庫 / 儲存庫 /
版本庫). Keeping the English original on first mention removes the ambiguity
without forcing readers to guess which translation the author meant. It also
keeps the page grep-able for English search terms.

`add-language.sh` and `add-docs-page.sh` inject this rule as an admonition
at the top of every non-default-language stub so authors see it before they
start translating.

## What `add-language.sh` does, step by step

For users who want to apply pieces by hand or audit what the script touched:

1. **Locates `mkdocs.yml`** by walking up from CWD.
2. **Detects existing i18n state.** `yq` query against `.plugins[]` checks
   for an `i18n:` map.
3. **Inserts or extends `plugins.i18n`.**
   - If absent: prepends a fresh i18n block before `search`, with
     `[default-lang, new-lang]` as the language list.
   - If present and the new locale isn't there: appends to
     `plugins[].i18n.languages`.
   - If the locale is already present: no-op.
4. **Sets `theme.language`** to the default language if not already set
   (`mkdocs-static-i18n` warns when `theme.language` is missing).
5. **Walks `docs/`** for `*.md` files (excluding `_snippets/` and `assets/`),
   and for each non-locale-suffixed source page, creates a sibling
   `*.<LANG>.md` from `assets/translation-stub.md.template`.
6. **Updates `.skills/preferences.yaml`** with three keys:
   `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages` (ordered list, default first),
   `keep_english_terms: true`, `i18n_structure: suffix`.
7. **Un-comments `mkdocs-static-i18n>=1.2`** in `pyproject.toml`. If the
   line isn't there at all, prints a hint asking you to add it manually.

The script is idempotent: re-running with the same `--lang` is a no-op.

## `theme.language` vs plugin `languages`

These are two different things:

- [`theme.language`](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/setup/changing-the-language/)
  is **Material's UI strings** (search placeholder, "Edit this page", footer
  navigation hints). One value site-wide. Material ships translations for
  ~70 locales out of the box.
- `plugins.i18n.languages` is **content translation**. A list. Each entry
  declares a locale that has translated `*.<lang>.md` files.

You almost always want `theme.language` set to your default content language
so the UI matches when readers land on a default-language page.

## `nav_translations`

To translate section titles in the nav (e.g. `Workflows` → `工作流程`), use
`mkdocs-static-i18n`'s per-language `nav_translations`:

\```yaml
plugins:
  - i18n:
      docs_structure: suffix
      languages:
        - locale: en
          name: English
          default: true
        - locale: zh-TW
          name: 繁體中文 (zh-TW)
          nav_translations:
            Workflows: 工作流程
            Reference: 參考資料
\```

`add-language.sh` does **not** populate `nav_translations` for you —
section names are project-specific and translating them is a deliberate
authorial choice. Add them by hand once you have section titles to translate.

## Interaction with `llmstxt` and `copy-to-llm`

Two known limitations of the current setup:

- **`mkdocs-llmstxt` is language-agnostic.** It picks up every `.md` file,
  including `*.zh-TW.md` siblings. The generated `/llms.txt` and
  `/llms-full.txt` will contain both languages interleaved. There's no
  out-of-the-box way to produce per-language `llms.txt` files. If you need
  it, drop `llmstxt` for non-default languages or post-process its output.
- **`mkdocs-copy-to-llm` button text is English-only.** The "Copy to LLM" /
  "Open in ChatGPT" / "Open in Claude" labels stay in English on `zh-TW`
  pages. Customising them requires forking the plugin's CSS/JS — out of
  scope for this skill.

These don't break the build; they're cosmetic. Document the limitation in
your project's README if your audience is monolingual zh-TW.

## Removing a language

To remove `zh-TW` later:

1. Delete the `zh-TW` entry from `plugins[].i18n.languages` in `mkdocs.yml`.
2. (Optional) Delete every `*.zh-TW.md` file under `docs/`.
3. Update `.skills/preferences.yaml`:
   \```bash
   bash scripts/check-preferences.sh \
     --set 'mkdocs_site_bootstrap.languages=["en"]'
   \```
4. If you only had two languages and want to fully remove the plugin, also
   delete the `i18n:` block and re-comment `mkdocs-static-i18n` in
   `pyproject.toml`.

## Reset path

If you want to fully back out of all the i18n decisions and start over:

\```bash
bash scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset mkdocs_site_bootstrap
# Then manually revert mkdocs.yml / pyproject.toml as above, and
# re-run init-docs-site.sh or add-language.sh from scratch.
\```

The `--reset` clears the recorded decision; the agent will re-interview on
the next invocation.

## Future work — `i18n_structure: folder`

The `i18n_structure` preference key exists, but `add-language.sh` currently
only implements `suffix`. If we add `folder` later, the migration path will
be: walk `docs/`, move every default-language file into `docs/<default>/`,
move every `*.<lang>.md` into `docs/<lang>/<base>.md`, rewrite relative
links. Non-trivial — punted unless someone actually needs it.

```
